Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

one of phrase

a part of a group: one of them, many of us

also one of them, one of us, one of you, many of us, many of them, some of them, which of you, who of you, most of them, all of us, how many of you, three of us, of us, of you

classical

Liv. 2.13.6: Cloelia virgō ūna ex obsidibus

ūnus ex (ē, dē) + abl.

ūnus with ex, ē or dē and the ablative

one of (a group)

With ūnus, other numbers and quīdam, ex is commoner than the genitive: ūnus ex illīs, one of them; quīdam ex amīcīs, one of my friends.

Other words

  • genetīvus partītīvus (multī eōrum, nēmō vestrum) — of (the group a part is taken from): many of them, none of you

    construction: the genitive of the whole; of persons, nostrum, vestrum · classical · Sen. Ep. 58.22: nēmō nostrum; Liv. 1.56.10: quī vestrum prīmus

    After words of number and quantity: multī eōrum, many of them; plērīque agricolārum, most farmers; quis vestrum?, which of you? “Of us, of you” here is nostrum, vestrum; nostrī, vestrī are the object of a feeling (memor nostrī, mindful of us).

  • nōs omnēs, vōs paucī — all of us, few of you: when the number is the whole group

    construction: the number agrees with the pronoun, or with the verb’s person; no genitive · classical · Liv. 2.12.15: trecentī conjūrāvimus; Petr. 92.1: quot estis?

    When the number is the whole group, it agrees: nōs omnēs, all of us; trecentī conjūrāvimus, three hundred of us have sworn; Quot estis?, how many of you are there? The genitive of nōs omnēs is omnium nostrum.

Examples

  • Quis vestrum fenestram aperuit?

    Which of you opened the window?composed

  • Cloelia virgō ūna ex obsidibus … Tiberim trānāvit

    the girl Cloelia, one of the hostages, swam across the TiberLiv. 2.13.6

  • Ūnus autem ex illīs, ut vīdit quia mundātus est, regressus est

    and one of them, when he saw that he was healed, turned backVulg. Lc. 17.15–16

  • cum quīdam ex ejus adsentātōribus, Damoclēs, commemorāret in sermōne cōpiās ejus

    when one of his flatterers, Damocles, was talking of his wealthCic. Tusc. 5.61

  • plērīque agricolārum crēdidērunt

    most farmers have believedCol. 12.52.18

  • imperium summum Rōmae habēbit quī vestrum prīmus, ō juvenēs, ōsculum mātrī tulerit

    the highest power at Rome will be his who first of you, young men, kisses his motherLiv. 1.56.10

  • nēmō nostrum est īdem māne quī fuit prīdiē

    none of us is the same in the morning as he was the day beforeSen. Ep. 58.22

  • trecentī conjūrāvimus prīncipēs juventūtis Rōmānae ut in tē hāc viā grassārēmur

    three hundred of us, leading young men of Rome, have sworn to come at you in this wayLiv. 2.12.15

  • quot estis?

    how many of you are there?Petr. 92.1

  • est patria parēns omnium nostrum

    our country is the parent of us allCic. de Or. 1.196
